Les 100 Visages du Burkina Digital : Amon Bazongo, faire émerger une génération africaine de l'intelligence artificielle
items.description: À 43 jours de l'ouverture de Le Faso Digital 2026, nous poursuivons notre série consacrée aux femmes et aux hommes qui façonnent le Burkina numérique. Cent personnalités, cent parcours. Aujourd'hui, nous faisons uun arrêt sur Amon Mocé Rodolphe Bazongo, entrepreneur technologique, consultant en intelligence artificielle et bâtisseur de communautés, dont le parcours dessine des passerelles entre le Burkina Faso, l'Asie et les nouveaux territoires de l'innovation africaine. Il appartient à une génération qui n'a pas découvert le numérique avec Internet, mais qui a grandi avec lui. Une génération pour laquelle intelligence artificielle, blockchain, big data, startups ou économie spatiale ne relèvent plus de la science-fiction, mais constituent de nouveaux terrains d'apprentissage, d'entrepreneuriat et de développement. Chez Amon Bazongo, cette fascination pour les technologies émergentes s'accompagne toutefois d'une conviction : une révolution technologique n'a véritablement d'impact que lorsqu'un écosystème se forme autour d'elle. Former, connecter, entreprendre, expérimenter et créer des communautés : ces verbes racontent une bonne partie de son parcours. Du Burkina Faso à Taïwan, l'apprentissage de la technologie Le parcours académique d'Amon Bazongo commence au Burkina Faso. Après un baccalauréat scientifique, il intègre l'Université Polytechnique de Bobo-Dioulasso, où il obtient un DUT en ingénierie électrique et électronique. Sa trajectoire prend ensuite une dimension internationale avec son départ pour Taïwan. Il y étudie l'informatique à la National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, dans une filière d'élite, avant de poursuivre un master en Big Data Management à la Soochow University. Ces années asiatiques lui permettent de se former au contact d'un environnement technologique particulièrement dynamique, mais aussi d'acquérir une ouverture culturelle qui accompagnera la suite de son parcours. Son CV indique ainsi qu'il travaille en français et en anglais et possède également une maîtrise du mandarin chinois. De l'ingénierie logicielle à l'intelligence artificielle Sa carrière professionnelle débute également à Taïwan. Chez aPure Functional Fiber, il développe des applications marketing, des outils analytiques et des chatbots destinés à accompagner la stratégie numérique et commerciale de l'entreprise. Mais c'est progressivement vers l'intelligence artificielle que son parcours s'oriente. À partir de 2019, il intervient comme consultant IA auprès d'Intelliances. L'un des projets les plus significatifs est inCare, un système avancé d'intelligence artificielle appliqué à la cardiologie, conçu, développé et déployé en collaboration avec un hôpital de Kaohsiung à Taïwan. L'expérience illustre déjà une caractéristique de son parcours : l'IA n'y est pas envisagée uniquement comme un objet technique, mais comme une technologie pouvant trouver des applications concrètes dans des secteurs aussi stratégiques que la santé. Quand l'innovation rencontre l'Afrique Après l'Asie, le parcours d'Amon Bazongo se rapproche progressivement des grands enjeux de transformation numérique du continent. Entre janvier 2022 et janvier 2023, il rejoint la Commission de l'Union africaine comme Digital and Innovation Fellow. Il y propose notamment un système de recherche fondé sur l'intelligence artificielle afin d'améliorer la gestion interne des connaissances au sein de la Direction de l'information et de la communication. Cette expérience marque une autre étape : celle du passage de l'innovation technologique aux problématiques institutionnelles africaines. Parallèlement, il s'intéresse à l'investissement dans les startups. Sélectionné comme Investor Accelerator Fellow de Dream VC en 2023, il analyse et identifie des jeunes pousses africaines dans la santé, l'environnement, l'intelligence artificielle, la blockchain ou encore l'assurance. Il contribue également à des travaux sur l'e-mobilité et publie une analyse consacrée au capital-risque dans les secteurs de la blockchain et des cryptoactifs en Afrique. Tech Emerging Africa : créer l'écosystème avant d'attendre le marché Mais c'est probablement avec Tech Emerging Africa, créé en 2020, que se révèle le mieux la vision d'Amon Bazongo. L'initiative vise à fédérer les acteurs intéressés par l'intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes, à diffuser les connaissances et à créer des espaces où étudiants, chercheurs, entrepreneurs et professionnels peuvent se rencontrer. Sous cette bannière, Amon Bazongo organise notamment IndabaX Burkina ainsi que la Semaine de l'Intelligence Artificielle et des Technologies Émergentes (SEINAR). Des événements qui ont cumulé plus de 2 000 participants entre 2023 et 2025. Il participe également à l'organisation de l'Africa Tech Up Tour pour le Burkina Faso et l'espace AES et conduit la délégation burkinabè lors d'un bootcamp à Cotonou. Autant d'initiatives qui poursuivent un même objectif : faire en sorte que les jeunes Africains ne regardent pas les prochaines révolutions technologiques depuis les tribunes, mais puissent en devenir des acteurs. Faire entrer l'IA dans les salles de classe… et dans la compétition Cette ambition passe naturellement par la formation. À travers Brain Machine & Consensus Burkina Faso, cabinet qu'il fonde en 2022, Amon Bazongo développe notamment une certification en intelligence artificielle et assure la formation de personnels de différentes organisations. Il anime également une newsletter professionnelle consacrée à l'IA, The AI-Aware Professional. Depuis novembre 2025, il conduit par ailleurs les initiatives liées à l'intelligence artificielle et à l'entrepreneuriat au Burkina Institute of Technology de Koudougou. Mais la transmission prend chez lui une forme plus originale encore : la compétition. Amon Bazongo organise les Olympiades nationales d'intelligence artificielle du Burkina Faso et siège à l'assemblée générale des Olympiades internationales d'intelligence artificielle. L'enjeu dépasse le concours lui-même. Il s'agit de détecter tôt les talents, de familiariser les jeunes avec les technologies de pointe et de créer une culture scientifique susceptible de faire émerger les ingénieurs et entrepreneurs de demain. De la communauté à l'entreprise Construire un écosystème technologique suppose également de transformer les idées en entreprises. Depuis 2025, Amon Bazongo développe au sein de Brain Machine & Consensus un startup studio, qui accueille plusieurs projets entrepreneuriaux, notamment Certify Magic, Cash Ma Chic et Africa Trade Connect. Il a également exercé les fonctions de directeur technique de Vester AI, une plateforme destinée à accompagner l'investissement dans les startups. Cette articulation entre formation, communautés, événements, investissement et incubation traduit une approche assez complète de l'écosystème numérique : il ne suffit pas de former des talents si ceux-ci ne disposent pas ensuite d'espaces pour expérimenter, entreprendre, financer leurs projets et accéder à des marchés. De l'intelligence artificielle… à l'espace Le champ d'intérêt d'Amon Bazongo ne s'arrête d'ailleurs pas à l'IA. Depuis 2024, il représente en Afrique de l'Ouest Cosmos For Humanity, une organisation engagée sur les questions de durabilité spatiale. Son périmètre couvre le Sahel et le golfe de Guinée. Cette incursion dans le domaine spatial peut sembler éloignée des autres activités de son parcours. Elle s'inscrit pourtant dans la même logique : anticiper les technologies et les secteurs qui structureront les économies futures et positionner les compétences africaines suffisamment tôt dans ces nouveaux espaces. Construire plutôt que subir les prochaines révolutions technologiques Le parcours d'Amon Bazongo porte finalement un message générationnel. L'intelligence artificielle, la blockchain, le big data ou les technologies spatiales sont largement développés hors du continent africain. Le risque serait que l'Afrique se contente une nouvelle fois de consommer des innovations conçues ailleurs. Son engagement dans la formation, l'organisation de communautés, l'entrepreneuriat et les compétitions technologiques défend une autre possibilité : préparer suffisamment tôt les talents africains pour qu'ils puissent eux aussi inventer, entreprendre et participer aux choix qui façonneront ces technologies. Cette ambition n'exclut pas les questions de responsabilité. Son CV mentionne notamment sa participation en 2024 à un panel de haut niveau consacré à la gouvernance des données et à une utilisation éthique, responsable et inclusive de l'intelligence artificielle. Car construire un écosystème de l'IA ne signifie pas seulement apprendre à créer des algorithmes. Il faut aussi apprendre à interroger leurs usages et leurs conséquences. Pourquoi fait-il partie des 100 Visages du Burkina Digital ? Parce qu'il fait partie d'une génération d'entrepreneurs technologiques burkinabè dont les parcours et les réseaux dépassent largement les frontières nationales. Parce qu'il travaille depuis plusieurs années à créer autour de l'intelligence artificielle un véritable écosystème associant formation, événements, communautés, entrepreneuriat et investissement. Parce qu'à travers Tech Emerging Africa, IndabaX Burkina, la SEINAR et les Olympiades nationales d'intelligence artificielle, il contribue à rapprocher les technologies émergentes des jeunes et des professionnels burkinabè. Parce que son parcours entre le Burkina Faso, Taïwan, la Chine et l'Union africaine lui permet de faire circuler expériences, compétences et opportunités entre plusieurs écosystèmes technologiques. Et parce qu'il porte une conviction essentielle pour l'avenir du continent : face aux prochaines révolutions technologiques, l'Afrique ne doit pas attendre d'être invitée. Elle doit former ses talents, construire ses communautés, créer ses entreprises et prendre sa place autour de la table. www.lefasodigital.net

items.title: Elections 2026 : El Mansouri défend les compétences du PAM et tacle ses rivaux
items.description: Le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) a choisi de lancer la campagne de ses grands rassemblements nationaux en vue des prochaines échéances législatives depuis Berkane, dans la région de l'Oriental. Devant une assistance de plus de 3.000 sympathisants, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, coordinatrice nationale de la direction collégiale du PAM, a livré une prestation incisive, cadrant les ambitions politiques de sa formation, défendant les récentes adhésions de personnalités d'envergure et répliquant vivement aux critiques des adversaires politiques. Soulignant que le choix de Berkane n'avait rien d'un hasard compte tenu du positionnement stratégique et de la symbolique politique de l'Oriental, El Mansouri a tenu à recadrer le débat sur l'attractivité du parti. Réagissant à la polémique suscitée par le ralliement de figures politiques et institutionnelles de premier plan, elle a affirmé que les discussions au sein du bureau politique n'ont jamais porté sur la quête de postes ou de privilèges, mais sur la mobilisation de compétences opérationnelles. Évoquant explicitement l'adhésion de Fouzi Lekjaa, elle a rappelé la proximité historique et la convergence de convictions démocrates-sociales qui lient le dirigeant au projet du PAM, insistant sur le fait que le parti privilégie désormais l'action de terrain aux discours abstraits. Face aux accusations de débauchage formulées par d'autres formations, la responsable politique s'est inscrite en faux, assurant que le PAM « n'engrange personne contre sa volonté » et que ces migrations politiques relèvent de choix individuels assumés. A cet égard, elle n'a pas manqué d'ironiser sur la nervosité de la concurrence, estimant que la dynamique actuelle du parti du tracteur en a « effrayé plus d'un » . Elle a rappelé au passage l'inconsistance des attaques de certains rivaux qui, lors des scrutins de 2016 et 2021, avaient eux-mêmes absorbé plusieurs parlementaires issus des rangs du PAM sans que cela ne donne lieu à des lamentations publiques. Pour ce qui est de l'offre électorale, El Mansouri a invité les électeurs à sanctionner les acteurs politiques sur la base de leur bilan effectif et de leur capacité à tenir leurs engagements, invitant chacun à « assumer ses propres échecs » . Elle a mis en avant un programme électoral structuré et transversal, citant notamment des propositions sociales concrètes comme l'attribution de l'intégralité de la pension de retraite aux veuves. Rejetant catégoriquement la logique des privilèges et du népotisme administratif, elle a conclu en rappelant son devoir d'équité gouvernementale envers toutes les collectivités territoriales, quelle que soit leur couleur politique, scellant son intervention par un engagement d'éthique et de fidélité envers les électeurs. items.title: Burkina/Mémorial Thomas Sankara : Le ministère de la Guerre annonce une contribution de 5 millions de FCFA
items.description: BURKINA-HOMMAGE-THOMAS-SANKARA Burkina/Mémorial Thomas Sankara : Le ministère de la Guerre annonce une contribution de 5 millions de FCFA Ouagadougou, 3 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Le ministre d’État, ministre chargé de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le Général de division Célestin Simporé, a annoncé, jeudi, une contribution de son département à hauteur de 5 millions de FCFA pour accompagner le projet de construction du mémorial Thomas Sankara. « Ce rendez-vous de la Nation n’est pas seulement un devoir de mémoire, il est aussi une affirmation renouvelée de nos engagements pour la dignité, la souveraineté et la justice sociale », a déclaré le ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, Célestin Simporé. Présidant la 11e cérémonie d’hommage au père de la Révolution et à ses douze compagnons, le camarade Simporé a annoncé une contribution de son département de 5 millions de FCFA pour la construction du Mémorial du père de la Révolution burkinabè, le Capitaine Thomas Sankara. Saisissant l’occasion, il a présenté l’ancien Président du Faso, le Capitaine Thomas Sankara, comme une figure de l’émancipation collective et de la volonté du peuple burkinabè de reprendre en main son destin. Célestin Simporé a également rappelé les idéaux associés à son action, notamment la promotion des droits de l’homme, l’émancipation de la femme, l’accès à l’éducation et à la santé, la lutte contre la corruption et la construction d’un État au service du peuple. Selon lui, ces valeurs doivent continuer d’orienter l’action publique et les efforts en faveur des populations. Il a invité les Burkinabè à puiser dans cet héritage pour faire face aux défis auxquels le pays est confronté. « Que sa mémoire inspire notre réflexion, éclaire nos décisions et guide nos efforts pour une patrie libre, digne et prospère », a-t-il confié. Le Général de division Célestin Simporé a également salué l’engagement des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) et des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), pour les efforts qu’ils consentent au quotidien, au péril de leur vie, pour la reconquête de l’intégrité du territoire national. Le ministre d’État a enfin souhaité que les idéaux de la Révolution d’août 1983 soient une source d’inspiration pour la Révolution progressiste populaire portée par le président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Agence d’information du Burkina LID-SAM/yos

items.title: NECO exam questions sold for N3,000 before papers – Alausa
items.description: Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has revealed that National Examinations Council (NECO) examination questions were allegedly sold for N3,000 before candidates sat for the papers. Alausa made the disclosure on Thursday during a meeting with the National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools and other stakeholders in the education sector. He described the level of examination malpractice in Nigeria as “mind-boggling”, warning parents, teachers, school proprietors, principals, invigilators and students against practices capable of undermining the integrity of public examinations. The minister said examination malpractice had been tolerated for years, creating an unfair environment in which students who prepared adequately were disadvantaged by candidates who gained access to examination questions before the tests. According to him, the practice could also encourage honest students to engage in malpractice in an attempt to compete with those who had access to leaked examination materials. Alausa said, “It’s sad. Before she and I came, the acceptance of examination malpractice, cheating and examination leakages in this country was mind-boggling, and the country accepted it. It was a nightmare,” adding that the “danger was that the good students would also become bad.” Recounting his experience in tackling examination malpractice, the minister alleged that examination questions had previously been available for sale before candidates sat for their papers. He said, “The Registrar of NECO at the time had a name. His name was Wushishi. You would go to Wushishi… I didn’t know that Wushishi meant going to the dark website. “They bought his question for N3,000. That was it. Before the examination. They called him Wushishi and bought the questions for N3,000 before the examination.” The minister also recounted what he described as a difficult period during the 2025 examinations, when he was allegedly sent questions before candidates sat for the relevant papers. He said officials were forced to verify the materials with examination authorities, sometimes discovering that the questions being circulated were the same ones scheduled for the day. He said, “During that examination period, during the hardest time of my life, I was always worried, waking up. I would wake up to her text. She would send questions to me… She would say, ‘I just got this question.’ “It could be English or Chemistry. I was always waking up with trepidation every morning, doing work. I would send it to the HNO and ask, ‘HNO, is this correct?’ And the answer I got was, ‘Unfortunately, that’s the question we’re doing today.’ “So, that was a more aggressive intervention because we were seeing the question and confirming from the other side.” Alausa said examination malpractice could not be treated as a problem caused solely by students, stressing that the wider education ecosystem must take responsibility for curbing the practice. He identified parents, school owners, teachers, invigilators and principals as key stakeholders whose actions could either prevent or facilitate access to examination materials. The minister said, “You might be in that isolated school, but the school system is also involved. In fact, I don’t blame the students that much. Any child can be bad. “But when we have an ecosystem where parents, schools, teachers, invigilators and principals are in full connivance, the students are the smallest players. The people who should put the deterrents in place are the ones involved.” He warned that the Federal Government would intensify measures aimed at protecting the credibility of public examinations and ensuring that academic qualifications reflected genuine learning and merit. Alausa said the reforms were part of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s broader efforts to raise standards and reposition the education sector. He said, “What are we doing? Desecrating the Nigerian system? It won’t happen. Not under the watch of this President. “This is a country with rule of law. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is transforming this country in a way that’s never been transformed before. This is Nigeria renaissance that we’re building to be sustainable into the future.” He said the country had tolerated practices that weakened its education system for too long, but insisted that the Tinubu administration was determined to reverse the trend. Minister of State for Education, Prof Suwaiba Ahmad, also urged private school proprietors and other education stakeholders to support the government’s reforms. Ahmad noted that tighter examination controls could initially expose weaknesses in students’ actual academic preparation. She explained that some students who appeared to perform exceptionally well in internal examinations might have become accustomed to accessing leaked questions before external examinations. According to her, the introduction of serialised examination questions would make it more difficult for candidates to depend on leaked materials and encourage students to prepare genuinely for their examinations. The post NECO exam questions sold for N3,000 before papers – Alausa appeared first on Vanguard News .

Le Sénégal mise sur la prévention et une alimentation plus saine
items.description: La lutte contre les maladies non transmissibles passe aussi par l’assiette. C’est la conviction du ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, Dr Ibrahima Sy. Il a pris part, ce jeudi 3 septembre 2026, à l’atelier de mise à niveau du Conseil municipal de Dakar consacré aux maladies non transmissibles liées à l’alimentation et à l’étiquetage des denrées alimentaires. Organisée par la Ville de Dakar dans le cadre du projet « Dakar PHC – Partnership for Healthy Cities », la rencontre vise à renforcer l’implication des élus locaux dans la promotion d’une alimentation favorable à la santé. Il s’agit notamment de permettre aux consommateurs de mieux identifier la composition des produits alimentaires, particulièrement leur teneur en sel, en sucre et en matières grasses. Nécessité de conjuguer les efforts Au cours de cette rencontre, le ministre de la Santé a insisté sur la nécessité d’une mobilisation collective pour faire face à la progression des maladies non transmissibles. L’État, les collectivités territoriales et les partenaires sont ainsi appelés à conjuguer leurs efforts pour renforcer la prévention contre l’hypertension artérielle, le diabète, les maladies cardiovasculaires et les maladies rénales chroniques. Au-delà de l’information des consommateurs, l’enjeu est de favoriser des environnements alimentaires plus sains. L’étiquetage apparaît, dans cette perspective, comme un outil permettant aux populations de mieux connaître les produits qu’elles consomment et d’opérer des choix plus éclairés. L’initiative accorde également une attention particulière aux enfants et aux personnes vulnérables, davantage exposés aux conséquences d’une alimentation déséquilibrée. Pour les autorités sanitaires, la prévention demeure un levier essentiel pour réduire à terme le poids des maladies non transmissibles sur les populations et sur le système de santé. A.N

items.title: Computers Promised to Free Us. What Happened?
items.description: This is an edition of Time-Travel Thursdays, a journey through The Atlantic ’s archives to contextualize the present. Sign up here. During the 1984 Super Bowl, an advertisement launched a technological revolution. If you were alive, you probably know the one. Directed by Ridley Scott, the minute-long spot showed men in gray uniforms, heads shaved, eyes blank, marching in unison toward a lifeless auditorium. A Big Brother figure speaks from a giant screen, droning on about “the first glorious anniversary of the Information Purification Directives.” All the while, a woman in red shorts and a white tank top is running to the auditorium. She looks like she’s just come from an aerobics class, but she has a sledgehammer, and authorities are in pursuit. Entering the room, she hurls the sledgehammer into Big Brother’s face. There’s a flash of light, and a wind blows over the stunned, awakened audience. A different voice—a comforting one—announces, “On January 24th, Apple Computer will introduce Macintosh. And you’ll see why 1984 won’t be like 1984 .” Although the ad did not show an actual Macintosh computer, it worked. Apple went on to sell 250,000 of its user-friendly, mouse-driven little machines in that year alone. The ad also asserted what was to be a defining idea of the emerging digital age: that personal computers, far from massive instruments of centralized control, were vessels of individual freedom. The coming of the internet, with its invitation to universally accessible knowledge and the free exchange of ideas, seemed to affirm the promise: Our machines wouldn’t enslave us; they would liberate us. The dystopia depicted in the ad came by way of George Orwell’s imagination, but the fears underlying it had deep American roots. As mass consumer culture expanded in the early 20th century, American artists, intellectuals, and critics worried over the problem of “conformity” and the loss of individualism that came with it. Most didn’t see the dark totalitarianism of 1984 ; instead, they saw a world of ready-made desires, a soulless existence brought to you by corporations, advertisers, media, and politicians. As The Atlantic ’s review of Sinclair Lewis’s Babbitt put it in 1922, “the ‘standardized American’” was becoming “as much a national product as the Ford car”—a person like Babbitt himself, whose entire life and very personality were shaped by forces beyond him. Such criticism formed a fault line that ran from the cultural commentary of the ’20s to the outbursts of Beats , folkies, and academics in the ’50s. The earthquake, of course, would come in the counterculture of the 1960s. No longer would people need to be stuffed into “ Little Boxes ,” as the folk singer Malvina Reynolds worried early in the decade. The counterculture promised liberation from such confinement. Visiting San Francisco’s Haight-Ashbury district for The Atlantic in 1967, the novelist Mark Harris wondered whether he was seeing Babbitt’s descendants finally rebelling against conformity in ways that Babbitt himself could not. The counterculture’s sensibilities migrated into the mainstream, where popular culture and advertising absorbed its language of liberation and transgression, so that admen could pitch 7 Up using hippie iconography or Virginia Slims cigarettes by way of the women’s-liberation movement. Digital culture would prove especially receptive to these countercultural ideals. Northern California, after all, was the center of both the counterculture and the tech industry, and the cross-pollination between the two was considerable, as the historian Fred Turner has shown . By the 1990s, as the internet was becoming a mass medium, some of its first boosters (many of whom had roots in the counterculture) were presenting it as the realization of countercultural ideals. John Perry Barlow, a poet and sometimes Grateful Dead lyricist, wrote his 1996 “Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace” in response to an early effort to regulate the internet. It reads like a Port Huron Statement for digital culture, describing a realm of individual freedom and free-flowing ideas that would break from existing forms of cultural and institutional authority. According to Barlow, a new “civilization of the Mind” was coming. In the dot-com and digital revolutions that followed, many of the people who sold the hardware, coded the software, and built the platforms were seen as iconoclasts themselves. Digital entrepreneurship became a form of transgression, not just in the casual dress and informal culture of the Silicon Valley office but also in what it promised to users. Tech visionaries pledged to create a world that would make possible precisely the kind of self-expression, open exchange, and communal connection that the counterculture had promised. It was no coincidence that by the late 1990s, Apple’s advertising—again with almost no reference to the machines themselves—simply pictured groundbreaking figures such as Gandhi, Martin Luther King Jr., Bob Dylan, and John Lennon, alongside the slogan “ Think Different .” In many ways, those promises were fulfilled. The internet did splinter 20th-century mass culture, and the effects have been every bit as revolutionary as promised. We don’t all watch the same networks anymore; we don’t see the same movies; we don’t get our news from the same places or read the same books ( mostly, we just don’t read ); we “ do our own research .” Even as the conditions of mass culture and conformity that shaped the counterculture and the early dreams of the internet have faded, we continue to live in their shadow. In the fractured age of social media and the unknowable algorithm, our devices give us the feeling of freedom, even as they serve the interests of corporate forces that track our movements, catalog our interests, and profile our wants. The oppressive monoculture has been replaced by countless minicultures, each with their own devoted acolytes; we still inhabit little boxes, partially of our own making. The transgressive ethos, meanwhile, continues to thrive. Subversion is perhaps the dominant language of digital culture, spoken across the political spectrum by podcasters “just asking questions,” wellness gurus swilling at-home health hacks, manosphere kingpins lashing out against wokeness, and lefty influencers denouncing the billionaire class. Everyone, it seems, is hurling a sledgehammer at something.

items.title: Sudanese anti-war forces reject AU backing for El Burhan dialogue
items.description: Sudanese anti-war political and civil forces have rejected the African Union’s endorsement of a “Sudanese-Sudanese Dialogue Initiative” proposed by Sovereignty Council President and Commander-in-Chief of the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) Lt Gen Abdelfattah El Burhan, warning that the process could legitimise military rule and deepen Sudan’s division. In a memorandum submitted on September 2 to the African Peace and Security Council and the AU Political Affairs, Peace and Security Commission, the groups rejected the AU Commission’s August 31 statement welcoming the initiative . They said the endorsement contradicted the Peace and Security Council’s position that a humanitarian truce should lead to an immediate and comprehensive ceasefire before any political process. They also criticised the AU for backing an initiative proposed by El Burhan, whose October 2021 military coup resulted in Sudan’s suspension from AU activities. The groups stressed that dialogue itself was not the problem but argued that any credible political process must be genuinely Sudanese-owned, with participants, agenda and timing agreed by Sudanese stakeholders. They called for the humanitarian crisis and cessation of hostilities to remain at the centre of the process. A group photo of members of the Sudanese-Sudanese Dialogue Committee after the committee’s press conference in Khartoum on Sunday, August 30, 2026 (Photo: Social media) They also demanded the exclusion of the National Congress Party, the Islamic Movement and affiliated forces, which they accused of playing a documented role in starting and prolonging the war. The memorandum warned that holding dialogue in territory controlled by one side of the conflict, without a prior ceasefire or broad participation, could entrench the political and territorial fragmentation created by the war. The groups called on the AU to explain its endorsement, reaffirm its ceasefire-first position, maintain neutrality and coordinate international mediation efforts, including the Quartet and Quintet mechanism. The AU Commission said its support was based on the need for an inclusive process involving Sudanese civil, political and societal actors. It said the dialogue should ultimately lead to a united, sovereign Sudan governed by legitimate civilian institutions, with a single national security structure and peaceful mechanisms for resolving political differences. Othman Mirghani, spokesman for the Sudanese-Sudanese Dialogue Committee, welcomed the AU statement, saying it came at a crucial stage as the committee began its work. Speaking to Radio Dabanga, Mirghani said regional backing could help secure wider international support while preserving the committee’s independence. He said the initiative sought direct dialogue among Sudanese inside the country and that the AU could help facilitate contacts with the UN, United States, UK and European Union. The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces aligned-government, Sudan Founding Alliance (Tasees) , also rejected the AU endorsement, describing it as support for the army’s position and bias towards one side of the conflict. Tasees spokesperson Ahmed Tagad Lisan said El Burhan had called for the dialogue, formed its preparatory committee and determined its agenda and venue, giving the SAF’s leadership undue influence over the process. The anti-war forces reiterated that they remain open to dialogue but insisted that a credible process must first stop the fighting, protect civilians and prevent the war from being used to legitimise competing centres of power. items.title: Incident concours directs session 2026 : Le Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple rassure les candidats
items.description: La commission nationale de pilotage des concours était face à la presse dans l’après-midi du jeudi 3 septembre 2026, au sein des locaux du Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple, à Ouagadougou. Au menu, l’incident relatif aux résultats d’admissibilité aux concours directs de recrutement des élèves de cycle C de l'Institut des finances publiques (IFPB) (ex-ENAREF, cycle C) et des élèves gestionnaires des services de santé, session 2026. Au cours de cette conférence de presse, il s’est agi pour la commission, d’expliquer aux femmes et hommes de médias, la raison de la rectification des communiqués portant résultat d'admissibilité desdits concours et de rassurer l'ensemble des candidates et candidats et l'opinion publique de la crédibilité du processus de l'organisation des concours de la fonction publique. Parlant de l'incident, le Camarade Suanyaba Rodrigue OBOULBIGA, président de la commission nationale de pilotage des concours, a rappelé que suite aux préoccupations relatives à une éventuelle non prise en compte des copies du centre de composition de Koudougou, des vérifications ont été menées par les techniciens et ont abouti au constat d'une prise en compte partielle des copies dudit centre de composition. « Au regard de ce constat, toutes les délibérations en cours ont été suspendues. Un contrôle approfondi sur les données de correction de tous les concours dont les résultats avaient déjà été publiés et ceux dont les résultats étaient en phase de délibération ou de vérification a été engagé. C’est ce contrôle approfondi d’ensemble qui a permis de constater, dans ce même centre de composition de Koudougou, une prise en compte partielle des copies du concours direct de recrutement de cinquante-trois (53) élèves gestionnaires des services de santé. Hormis ces deux concours, les vérifications ont montré que toutes les copies scannées de l’ensemble des centres de composition avaient été corrigées », a-t-il ajouté. Pour le Camarade Oboulbiga, l’incident relatif à ces deux concours relève d’une erreur humaine. « Le problème s'est posé lors du transfert des copies, issues du groupage, vers les postes de correction. Une comparaison entre le nombre de copies de la source, qu'est la machine de groupage, et le nombre de copies déposées sur la machine de correction aurait permis de déceler le transfert partiel des copies. On peut donc affirmer, sans risque de se tromper, qu'il s'agit d'une erreur humaine et non d'une défaillance du dispositif de correction électronique », a-t-il indiqué. Pour garantir l’égalité de chances des candidats à ces concours, le Camarade président de la commission nationale de pilotage a souligné que les copies non prises en compte ont été immédiatement corrigées et les candidats admissibles intégrés parmi ceux initialement déclarés admissibles. La commission a tenu à rassurer que les copies des candidats de tous les centres de composition ont été scannées, corrigées et prises en compte dans la délibération des résultats et que les responsabilités seront situées. A la suite de la déclaration liminaire, la commission s’est prêtée aux questions des femmes et hommes de média en vue de lever toute équivoque autour de l’incident. DCRP/MSP Minute.bf

items.title: ICPC sacks security officer over unauthorised access granted El-Rufai’s wife
items.description: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has dismissed a security officer accused of helping Aichatou Assabe El-Rufai, one of the wives of former Kaduna State governor Nasir El-Rufai, gain unauthorised access to him while he was in custody. Daniel Stephen, who was attached to the commission’s internal security team, was allegedly caught on CCTV assisting Assabe to enter the ICPC premises on July 5, 2026, outside the approved visitor access procedure. Stephen reportedly admitted his involvement in a handwritten statement submitted to an investigation panel, according to The Cable. In the statement, he acknowledged helping El-Rufai’s wife gain access to her husband “through the back door”. Stephen is said to have driven Assabe into the commission’s premises, taken her through the back entrance and escorted her upstairs to the section where El-Rufai was being held. “At one point, according to his handwritten account, he turned off the light before they went into the room where El-Rufai was,” an ICPC officer was quoted as saying. “Mrs El-Rufai handed her husband a document, picked up a black purse and spoke with him in Hausa about a court matter. The visit lasted about 15 minutes. “Stephen said he then took her out through the same back entrance and drove her out of the commission’s premises.” Stephen reportedly told the panel that he was aware the visit had not complied with the commission’s established security procedures. He explained that visitors to the ICPC premises were required to have their details recorded at the gate and obtain clearance from the head of the security unit before being allowed into the facility. The officer also admitted that his actions amounted to a breach of the commission’s rules. “I agree that I am wrong and breached commission procedure,” he wrote, adding that he made the statement voluntarily and without coercion or duress. ICPC insiders were said to have further claimed that Stephen’s account suggested his involvement with Assabe extended beyond the July 5 incident. Stephen allegedly recounted an earlier encounter in which he helped escort her further into the facility while officials were still confirming her identity and that after assisting her, he was approached by a man who identified himself as El-Rufai’s blood brother. According to his account, he also agreed to assist the man and brought him into the facility through the back entrance. El-Rufai has been in ICPC custody since February 19, following his release by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). He is being held on charges of money laundering and conversion of public property, which he denies. The post ICPC sacks security officer over unauthorised access granted El-Rufai’s wife appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Législatives : le parquet de Kénitra ouvre une enquête après des déclarations d'un candidat
items.description: Après des déclarations d'un responsable politique sur la supposée utilisation de fonds issus de la vente de drogue pour influencer les urnes lors des élections législatives attendues à la fin de ce mois, la Cour d'appel de Kénitra, a décidé d'ouvrir une enquête judiciaire. Dans un communiqué consulté par Hespress FR , le procureur général du Roi près la Cour d’appel de Kénitra a indiqué que l'enquête ouverte visera à déterminer les circonstances et les éléments entourant les déclarations attribuées à un candidat aux prochaines élections et à prendre les mesures juridiques nécessaires. Ces déclarations ont été diffusées sur certains réseaux sociaux, elle faisaient état d'une déclaration d’un candidat aux prochaines élections législatives lors d’un rassemblement partisan, selon laquelle « une importante quantité de drogues pourrait être utilisée, et les fonds issus de sa vente serviraient à influencer le processus électoral ». « Cette démarche s’inscrit dans le cadre du rôle dévolu au parquet pour veiller au bon déroulement du processus électoral, ainsi qu’au respect de la loi et à l’intégrité des opérations électorales », a indiqué le communiqué. items.title: History made! Accra Academy book first-ever NSMQ final Spot after dominant semi-final display
items.description: Accra Academy has qualified for the National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) Grand Finale for the first time in the school’s history. The Accra-based school secured the historic qualification after winning a fiercely contested semi-final on Thursday, September 3, 2026. The “Bleoo” boys finished with 5 4 points, ahead of Bright Senior High School’s 44 points and Achimota School’s 43 points. The result marks a significant milestone for Accra Academy, which has participated in the country’s premier academic competition for years but had never previously progressed to the Grand Finale. The semi-final contest remained closely fought as the three schools demonstrated strong knowledge and quick thinking across the various rounds. Achimota School mounted a spirited challenge, while Bright SHS also kept the contest competitive. Accra Academy, however, pulled clear in the final stages to secure the top spot and book its place in the ultimate contest. The historic qualification has sparked celebrations among students, old students and supporters of the school, with the achievement being hailed as a major moment in Accra Academy’s NSMQ history. Accra Academy will now join St. Augustine’s and PRESEC in the Grand Finale, where the 2026 NSMQ champion will be determined.

items.title: Grève des avocats : Ramid appelle à la trêve
items.description: Alors que l'Association des barreaux du Maroc maintient sa ligne dure, l'ancien ministre de la Justice El Mostafa Ramid a pris publiquement position en faveur d'une suspension de la grève des avocats. Dans un post sur sa page Facebook, il détaille les raisons pour lesquelles il juge la poursuite du mouvement contre-productive, sans pour autant dédouaner le gouvernement de sa gestion du dossier. El Mostafa Ramid s'est présenté en robe noire devant la Cour d'appel de Casablanca, puis a publié sur sa page Facebook un texte appelant les avocats à suspendre leur grève générale. Une position qui tranche avec la ligne officielle de l'Association des barreaux du Maroc (ABAM), toujours engagée dans le mouvement. Dans ce texte, Ramid avance plusieurs arguments pour justifier cette position. D'abord sur le calendrier : pour lui, prolonger la grève en pleine séquence électorale revient à s'acharner dans une impasse. Le pays traverse, d'après Ramid, un « temps mort » législatif où aucune négociation sérieuse n'est envisageable, rendant la mobilisation, en l'état, dénuée de sens. Sa recommandation est nette : suspendre le mouvement jusqu'à la formation du prochain gouvernement, puis rouvrir le dialogue sur des bases nouvelles. Ensuite sur le fond des revendications elles-mêmes. Ramid pointe un flou entretenu : le texte a été tant remanié depuis la mouture initiale du ministère de la Justice qu'il devient, dit-il, difficile de savoir précisément ce que les avocats acceptent encore et ce qu'ils rejettent. Il affirme ne pas avoir eu connaissance d'un document consensuel émanant des instances à l'origine de la grève, mais seulement de prises de position individuelles et regrette des dérapages sur les réseaux sociaux, qu'il juge incompatibles avec les usages de la profession. Sur le rapport de forces, son analyse est sans détour. Ramid estime que les avocats mènent « une confrontation déséquilibrée avec le gouvernement », une lutte menée sans soutien sociétal suffisamment large et dont l'issue, selon lui, est d'ores et déjà écrite. Il va plus loin en contestant la pertinence même de l'arme choisie. Pour lui, la grève ne pénalise pas les décideurs mais uniquement les justiciables et les avocats eux-mêmes, un raisonnement qu'il étaye d'un argument juridique : l'article 50 de la nouvelle loi, hérité de l'ancien texte, interdirait déjà tout engagement collectif de cessation totale d'activité envers la justice ; et l'article 21 de la loi organique sur le droit de grève imposerait un service minimum dans les secteurs vitaux, dont la justice fait partie. Deux obligations que le mouvement, selon lui, n'aurait pas respectées. C'est sans doute le point le plus sensible de sa sortie : Ramid juge inadmissible que des avocats cessent d'assister des personnes détenues dans des affaires pénales, rappelant que la défense doit rester du côté de la liberté, quelles que soient les circonstances, même face à une loi jugée injuste. Il dit craindre que les tribunaux ne prennent l'habitude de juger sans avocats, une pratique qui, si elle s'installait durablement, pourrait selon lui fragiliser la profession de façon irréversible. Il vise également certains confrères, dénonçant une contradiction qu'il juge problématique : des avocats affichés comme grévistes sur les réseaux sociaux tout en continuant, discrètement, à déposer leurs mémoires dans les dossiers en cours. Par ailleurs, et même si sa sortie vise avant tout la stratégie de l'ABAM, Ramid ne dédouane pas l'Exécutif pour autant. Il reconnaît que le gouvernement a mal géré ce dossier depuis le départ, pointant notamment des propos du ministre de la Justice qu'il juge blessants envers la profession et injustifiables. Cette prise de position a immédiatement suscité des réactions vives dans les rangs de la profession, où plusieurs voix contestent la lecture de l'ancien ministre, à un moment où l'Association des barreaux du Maroc maintient sa ligne dure : suspension totale des prestations, aide juridictionnelle comprise, et Assemblée extraordinaire prévue le 5 septembre à Rabat pour arrêter de nouvelles mesures. Le mouvement a désormais dépassé les 100 jours de paralysie judiciaire. The post Grève des avocats : Ramid appelle à la trêve appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Changements à la tête de la Radio algérienne et d’AL24news
items.description: La Radio algérienne et la chaîne publique AL24 News changent de tête. Pour la première, c’est Hicham Allali qui a été désigné comme nouveau directeur général en remplacement d’Adel Salakdji. Le nouveau patron de la radio publique a été installé dans ses fonctions ce jeudi 3 septembre par le ministre de la Communication, Mohamed Bouslimani, et le conseiller du président de la République chargé de la Direction générale de la communication, Kamel Sidi Said. Le journaliste Lamine Chikhi nommé DG d’AL24news Adel Salakdji était en poste depuis septembre 2024. Il avait succédé à Mohamed Baghali qui a été nommé directeur général de la Télévision algérienne (EPTV). En plus de la Radio algérienne, un nouveau directeur général a été désigné à la tête de la chaîne AL24 News. Il s’agit de Lamine Chikhi, journaliste qui a notamment travaillé comme correspondant de l’agence Reuters à Alger. Il remplace Ahmed Kateb qui était en poste depuis octobre 2025. Lamine Chikhi a été installé dans ses nouvelles fonctions par le directeur général de l'Anep. L’article Changements à la tête de la Radio algérienne et d’AL24news est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: The Hasan Piker Question
items.description: L ike late-summer humidity, Hasan Piker hangs heavy over the discourse. At a rally on Monday, Vice President Vance brought up the hard-left streamer in an attempt to paint the Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed as anti-American. Last week, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called Piker’s recent statements about Jewish Americans “dangerous and anti-Semitic.” Senators Jon Ossoff, Cory Booker, and Jacky Rosen said much the same. Facing questions about a totally different set of Piker comments, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez hustled into an elevator. Some Democrats are trying to dismiss the 35-year-old political commentator as irrelevant. He’s just “a streamer in California,” El-Sayed said on Saturday, waving off questions from reporters. Piker himself has spent the past week casting himself as the victim of hysteria. “I have become this media cycle’s ‘trans athletes’ or ‘migrant caravan,’” he posted on X. But it was El-Sayed who first made Piker central to his campaign by bringing him out on the trail, partying poolside with him at an influencer event, and celebrating with him during his Election Night rally. In his thousands of hours of streaming, Piker has produced a dense catalog of comments spanning the spectrum from stupid to incredibly offensive, including several iterations of the phrase “I hate America” and, perhaps most memorably, that “America deserved 9/11.” (He quickly attempted to walk it back .) Piker also flaunts his authoritarian sympathies, calling Mao Zedong “one of the great leaders of this world” and counting the collapse of the Soviet Union among the “catastrophes” of the 20th century. Last week, he warned that “eventually someone is going to come around and take action” against American Jews who are “singularly invested in Israel.” [ Read: What El-Sayed does next matters ] Hasan Piker is part of the conversation now. He has become central to the Republican strategy in Michigan, where El-Sayed will continue to be asked about him. So, too, will Democrats across the country. The question ahead of November is whether their answers will satisfy voters. E l-Sayed has moved away from Piker since winning the primary last month. The streamer has not been on the trail in Michigan. “I have spoken with the good doctor,” Representative Jim Clyburn told reporters of El-Sayed, who has a medical degree. “He has apologized. He says he will not campaign with Piker anymore.” After Piker’s comments last week about American Jews, El-Sayed said in a statement that anti-Semitism is a “scourge” and that “I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk.” When asked about Piker at a meeting with a group of Jewish Democrats on Saturday, though, El-Sayed declined to disavow him. “If you want to make this race about a streamer in California, I just think you’re missing the boat.” Anyone could have predicted the Piker blowback. Plenty of people did. In March, one of El-Sayed’s primary opponents, Mallory McMorrow, compared Piker to the white-supremacist influencer Nick Fuentes, and leaders of the centrist think tank Third Way wrote a column urging Democrats not to associate with Piker. “Everyone saw it coming from a mile away, so they should’ve been better prepared to handle it,” one Democratic strategist told me. Even some of El-Sayed’s own backers felt similarly. “Not all socialism is toxic to the Democratic brand, but Piker certainly is,” one progressive strategist told me. (None of the Democrat-aligned operatives I reached out to would agree to speak on the record for this story, citing their support for El-Sayed as well as their fear of reprisal from Piker’s rabid online fans.) The Piker drama is a ribbon-wrapped gift to Republicans in a year when so much else—inflation, high gas prices, an unpopular president—is working against them. They seem well aware of this. Mike Rogers, El-Sayed’s Republican opponent, refers to Piker as El-Sayed’s “running mate.” “When I see Abdul El-Sayed campaign around this state with somebody who said that America deserved 9/11, what I see is a man who has sympathy and compassion for people who share his religion, but has nothing for people who don’t,” Vance said at the rally on Monday. “What I’d ask you to remember is that whoever you send to Washington, whatever policy views you have or you don’t have, send people of good heart who focus on the right issues, who fight for the right people, and who love the United States of America.” The strategy is obvious: Identify every repellent thing Piker has ever said, tie Piker to El-Sayed, and advertise the relationship at every opportunity. There is more than a hint of irony in this situation. President Trump has shown a strong affinity for shock jocks and trolls. In 2020, he awarded Rush Limbaugh, who had a recurring segment celebrating the deaths of gay people from AIDS, the Presidential Medal of Freedom. Laura Loomer, a far-right activist and an ally of Trump’s, last week referred to a Senate candidate as a “ghetto black communist bitch.” Some Democrats, seeing Trump suffer little political consequence for such associations, believe it’s unfair that El-Sayed should have to answer for Piker’s actions. [ Read: Laura Loomer is a warning ] But politics, like life, is famously unfair. Democrats are constantly being asked to condemn Piker in cable-news hits and hallway interviews, even outside Michigan. Several Jewish Democrats have weighed in too. Through a spokesperson, Ossoff said he “unreservedly rejects reckless and dangerous rhetoric suggesting that policy advocacy invites violence against the Jewish community or any community.” Representative Josh Gottheimer of New Jersey said that “anyone who campaigns with Piker or elevates him is complicit in the rising antisemitism and anti-American hatred in this country.” Moderate Democrats are seizing the moment as a chance to engage in a little centrist posturing. Senator John Fetterman went on Fox News and delivered a challenge to El-Sayed: “I’m offering $50,000 for you to do a rally with Hasan Piker” on September 11, he said. Piker was not immediately available for comment for this story. But last week, after several Jewish Democrats criticized him, he dismissed their concerns by implying they reflected an orchestrated conspiracy against him, writing on X that an “aipac boss call was made.” Maybe El-Sayed could quell some of the frenzy himself. In 2008, controversial comments from Barack Obama’s former pastor Jeremiah Wright threatened to upend Obama’s bid for the White House. In a sermon shortly after September 11, the pastor said that “America’s chickens are coming home to roost.” Later, Wright said, “No, no, no, not God Bless America. God damn America—that’s in the Bible—for killing innocent people.” Obama chose to address the controversy directly, and delivered a speech condemning Wright’s remarks while offering context about America’s racial tensions. That speech “was a masterpiece of empathy, and at the time it felt that it changed the trajectory of his campaign,” Michelle Goldberg wrote this week. At the very least, some Democrats argue, El-Sayed could more plainly denounce his friend. “Say, ‘Here’s what I condemn; here’s what I disavow. I disagree; it was wrong and hurtful,’” the progressive strategist said. “If Piker says something new that’s bad—which, if I was a betting man, I’d say will happen—you come out against it swiftly.” Michigan, a state that Trump won in 2016 and 2024, was never going to be an easy win for El-Sayed. His relationship with Piker, who is paid to provoke, not persuade, isn’t going to make that task any simpler. The good news for Democrats is that most people don’t actually know Piker; polling from earlier this year showed that 60 percent of likely voters have never heard of him. The bad news for Democrats is that Republicans will spend the next two months working diligently to change that.

items.title: Woman’s decomposed body found in gutter near Haatso DVLA office
items.description: The body of a woman has reportedly been found in a gutter along the Haatso-Bohye Road near the New DVLA office. Residents are said to have been alerted by a strong stench from the area, prompting some of them to trace the source to the gutter where the body was discovered. The body was reportedly in an advanced state of decomposition, suggesting that it may have been there for some time before it was found. The discovery was subsequently reported to the police, who arrived at the scene to retrieve the body and begin investigations into the circumstances surrounding the death. The area was also fumigated following the removal of the body. Police have started investigations to establish the identity of the deceased and determine the circumstances that led to her unfortunate demise. Meanwhile, residents have appealed for streetlights to prevent further crimes.

items.title: « Tous voilés » : la riposte virale des Français au RN sur le voile
items.description: À l'approche des élections présidentielles en France , à laquelle va participer Marine Le Pen en tant que candidate, le Rassemblement National (RN) joue la carte de la lutte contre l’islamisme, désignant comme menace les femmes musulmanes voilées. Des activistes et des Français répondent en se couvrant la tête. Sur les réseaux sociaux, leurs vidéos sont devenues virales. C’est le député RN, Jean-Philippe Tanguy, qui a annoncé, le 30 août dernier, sur le plateau de BFMTV, que si la candidate de son parti, Marine Le Pen, arrive à l’Elysée, les femmes musulmanes portant le voile dans les espaces publics écoperont d’une amende. La mesure a été vite confirmée par le président du parti d’extrême droite, en l’occurrence Jordan Bardella, puis par la candidate à la présidentielle, Marine Le Pen, qui a déclaré qu’une fois à l'Elysée, elle allait soumettre aux Français, par référendum, une loi de lutte contre les idéologies islamistes, portant notamment sur « la pénalisation du voile islamiste dans l’espace public ». Contre le RN, des Françaises et des Français se couvrent la tête Face à cette démarche du RN, une large campagne de solidarité avec les femmes musulmanes a été lancée en France, notamment sur les réseaux sociaux, ou plusieurs internautes répondent, en silence, à l’obsession raciste et islamophobe du parti d’extrême droite. Sur Instagram, TikTok, Twitter, Facebook, on peut désormais rencontrer plusieurs vidéos où l’on voit des femmes, mais aussi des hommes, mettre le voile, en solidarité avec les femmes voilées musulmanes, mais surtout en réponse au projet du RN. Voir cette publication sur Instagram Une publication partagée par الجزيرة (@aljazeera) Cette démarche souligne surtout l’absurdité de la démarche du parti d’extrême droite qui vise à pénaliser des femmes pour le port d’un bout de tissu sur leur tête. “Maintenant, il faudra nous verbaliser tous”, écrit un internaute. Le projet du RN tourné en dérision Ces vidéos sont légion. Si certains internautes se filment sérieusement, d’autres tournent le projet du RN en dérision, comme ce jeune homme qui se filme avec un voile sur la tête expliquant que “son mari ne l’a pas forcé à le porter” ou encore cet autre homme qui assure qu’au “lendemain de l’interdiction du voile par le RN, il sortira dans la rue voilé”. @magfamilly3 #rn #voile #pourtoi #fyu #actualité ♬ son original – Mag&Djams Cet élan populaire sur les réseaux sociaux montre ainsi le caractère insensé du projet du RN qui a cependant réussi à détourner l’opinion publique de plusieurs sujets, comme celui de la condamnation, par la justice française, de sa candidate à la présidentielle pour détournement de fonds. L’article « Tous voilés » : la riposte virale des Français au RN sur le voile est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Residents of Akaa, surrounding communities demand improved network coverage
items.description: Residents of Akaa and several neighbouring communities in the Jasikan Municipality of the Oti Region are appealing to relevant authorities and telecommunications operators to address persistent network connectivity challenges in the area. Akaa Electoral Area Assembly Member, George Yeboah, popularly known as Teapot, said poor network coverage had become a major concern for residents, making it difficult for them to make telephone calls and communicate with relatives and other people in different parts of the country. According to Mr Yeboah, the challenge affects not only Akaa but also several surrounding communities within the electoral area. He listed the affected communities as Akaa Quarters, Akaa Adzamasi, Akaa Dzokpokofe, Akaa Bompa, Akaa Twingyina, Akaa Tankey and Akaa Kyrikasa. He said the unreliable network service was causing significant difficulties for residents and limiting effective communication across the communities. “Akaa Electoral Area is one of the largest towns here in the Jasikan Constituency. Network connectivity has been one of the major challenges we face in this area. We find it difficult to make calls or communicate with relatives and other people in different regions.” Mr Yeboah noted that residents in the neighbouring communities were facing the same problem, describing the situation as one that required urgent attention. “We are really suffering because of the poor network connectivity, and it is affecting communication in the area,” he said. The Assembly Member therefore called on the relevant authorities and telecommunications service providers, including MTN, Telecel and AirtelTigo, to intervene and improve network coverage in Akaa and the surrounding communities. He urged the providers to take concrete steps to strengthen their network infrastructure and ensure residents have reliable access to mobile communication services. Mr Yeboah said improved connectivity would ease communication difficulties faced by residents and help address the challenges created by the current poor network coverage. He appealed to the authorities and network operators to treat the concerns as a matter requiring urgent attention and work towards providing dependable telecommunications services to Akaa and the affected communities.

items.title: ‘Chief Justice’s role is to administer justice, not protect any agenda’ – Haruna replies Franklin Cudjoe
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) Deputy General Secretary, Haruna Mohammed, has pushed back against arguments that Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie merely stated the truth in his recent comments on the performance of state institutions. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Thursday, September 3, Mr Mohammed argued that the Chief Justice’s constitutional mandate is to administer justice and protect the independence of the Judiciary, rather than advance or safeguard the agenda of any political administration. Read also: Did he lie? I don’t see anything political about Chief Justice’s comments’ – Franklin Cudjoe His comments were in response to IMANI Africa President Franklin Cudjoe, who had argued that the Chief Justice may not have committed any wrongdoing in his comment on the performance of state institutions, dismissing suggestions that the remarks were politically motivated. Mr Mohammed disagreed. “Those who have said that the Chief Justice has said the truth certainly did not look at the facts very well. First, go and read Articles 12(5), 12(7)of the 1992 Constitution. The Chief Justice’s role is to administer justice. It is not the role of the Chief Justice to protect anybody’s agenda. That is out of it. That is not the work of the Chief Justice,” he pointed out. He said any indication that the Chief Justice is committed to ensuring that a particular government’s agenda succeeds could undermine the constitutional principle of judicial independence. According to Mr Mohammed, the Judiciary is expected to operate independently of the Executive, making it inappropriate for the Chief Justice to position himself as a protector of a political administration’s agenda. “If the Chief Justice says he’s going to protect and make sure that somebody’s agenda passes through, then definitely the Chief Justice has turned his back on the oath that he swore to protect and to administer justice for the good people of Ghana,” he said.

items.title: Zondoma : 120 acteurs honorés pour leurs engagements communautaires
items.description: Burkina/Zondoma-Distinctions-Acteurs-Communautaires Zondoma : 120 acteurs honorés pour leurs engagements communautaires Gourcy, 1er sept. 2026 (AIB) – Sous l’égide des « Initiatives Présidentielles pour le Développement Communautaire (IPDC) », des acteurs de la province du Zondoma ont été distingués, le samedi 29 août 2026, à Ouahigouya pour leurs engagements au service de leurs communautés. Ces acteurs se sont illustrés par leur engagement patriotique, notamment à travers des actions de développement au profit de leurs communautés dans les quatre provinces de la Région de Yaadga. C’est dans ce cadre qu’ils ont reçu des attestations de reconnaissance au cours d’une journée d’hommage et de reconnaissance organisée à Ouahigouya sous le patronage du gouverneur de la région de Yaadga, Thomas Yampa. Cette activité organisée par les « Initiatives présidentielles pour le développement communautaire (IPDC) » vise à valoriser l’apport des acteurs locaux qui, par leur disponibilité et leurs initiatives, contribuent à soutenir les communautés et à renforcer leurs résiliences dans la dynamique du développement endogène. Comme Oumarou Ouédraogo, Président de la Coordination provinciale des associations de la veille citoyenne du Zondoma, au moins 23 autres acteurs de la province intervenant dans divers domaines sont concernés par cette reconnaissance . Plus qu’une reconnaissance, ces distinctions sonnent comme une invite à toutes les filles et fils de la Région, chacun dans son domaine, à mettre la main dans la patte pour un véritable décollage socioéconomique de la région, dans un esprit de solidarité, de cohésion sociale et d’engagement patriotique. Au total, 120 personnes ont été distingués dans la Régions de Yaadga au titre de cette première édition. Agence d’Information du Burkina AK-DNK

items.title: Adamawa 2027: APC gov candidate not good politician, nobody knows him — Senator Abbo
items.description: Sekinat Osundiji Senator Elisha Ishaku Abbo, the 2027 Labour Party governorship candidate in Adamawa State, has described the governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) as a weak politician with little recognition in the state. Abbo made the remarks during an interview on Arise TV, where he expressed confidence that he would defeat the APC candidate in the upcoming governorship election. While acknowledging that his APC opponent was “a very good guy” and “a very gentleman,” Abbo argued that his lack of political visibility would work against him at the polls. “He is not a good politician, and he is not known by the people. Even in his village, people don’t know him. But I am like Coca-Cola; everybody knows me.” The former senator said his popularity, particularly among young people and poorer residents, gives him an advantage over other contenders in the election. Abbo also argued that the incumbent APC administration would be disadvantaged because, according to him, the state governor, Umaru Fintiri, was not allowed to choose the party’s governorship candidate. “In Adamawa State, my governor was pushed aside. He did not bring the candidate. Other people brought the governorship candidate and imposed him,” he said. According to Abbo, the situation represents a major political disadvantage for the ruling party ahead of the 2027 election. He further claimed that his political strength cuts across the three senatorial zones of Adamawa, saying he had previously won elections in Northern Adamawa under two different political parties. “I won election twice in Northern Adamawa. Twice, under two different political parties. The first in Adamawa State to do that,” he said. Abbo claimed he had already secured a strong base in the northern part of the state while also making inroads into the central and southern zones. “In Northern zone, I’m the only candidate. Central zone, there are four. So, I have my northern zone inside my pocket,” he said. He added that he had also gained support in parts of the central and southern zones, claiming that any candidate who secures eight local government areas would win the governorship election, while he already had nine “in his pocket.” Abbo, who repeatedly expressed confidence in his chances, concluded that he would emerge victorious in 2027. “I’ll win this election, Charles. Next time, after 2027, you’ll be interviewing a governor,” he told the interviewer. The post Adamawa 2027: APC gov candidate not good politician, nobody knows him — Senator Abbo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Top male and female cyclists from Africa and beyond will battle for the top prizes at the 7th edition of PRURide 2026 which takes place at Borteyman Highway on Sunday 6th September, 2026 at 12noon. The winners of the male and female Elite cyclist will each receive GH¢15,000, making the top prize a major attraction ahead of this year’s highly anticipated cycling event. The 2026 PRURide Elite Race, coming right after a successful 30km fun ride on UG campus will see the male category covering 112km and the female category covering 67.2km. The cash prize structure rewards the top 10 finishers in both the male and female categories. The first-place finishers (male and female) will each receive GH¢15,000, while second and third place will take home GH¢8,000 and GH¢5,000 respectively. Cyclists finishing between fourth and 10th position will also receive GH¢1,000 each. The incentives extend beyond the overall top finishers. The event will also recognise cyclists in several special categories, with GH¢1,000 allocated to each of the following: Oldest Male Rider (50 years and above), Oldest Female Rider (50 years and above), Youngest Male Rider (16–20 years), Youngest Female Rider (16–20 years), Person with Disability, Top three performing cycling clubs, GH¢1,000 each. Importantly, all participants will receive medals, ensuring that riders who take part in the race will leave with recognition for their participation. PRURide continues to bring together cyclists and cycling stakeholders as part of efforts to promote safe cycling and a green Ghana. PRURide 2026 is brought to you by Prudential Life Insurance Ghana, in partnership with the Ghana Cycling Federation, Ministry of Sports & Recreation, University of Ghana Sports & Wellness Directorate, National Sports Authority, National Road Safety Authority, Ghana Police Motor Traffic & Transport Department, Ghana Olympic Committee, Ghana Tourism Authority, Decathlon Ghana, Life Healthcare Centre, Aldin Cycles and produced by RITE Sports Services. items.title: Estonian defence minister resigns after €70m Ukraine munitions scam by Indian company: report
items.description: Estonian Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned following a scandal in which he authorised the payment of €70 million to an Indian company for artillery shells, only to receive ammunition of defective quality, it emerged on Thursday. Britain’s The Telegraph reported on Monday that Datasel SRL was contracted to produce the shells for use by the Ukrainian military against Russia, and that Datasel had “not previously produced or sold a single shell”. The newspaper says that Estonia made the payment from the EU military fund in August 2024 to send munitions to Ukraine’s front line by November that year. “The Indian-run, Italy-based company repeatedly delayed delivery. When a shipment was eventually inspected in 2025, the rounds were found to be faulty and none were sent to Ukraine,” The Telegraph reported. “The scandal is an embarrassment for Estonia, which has increased its military spending because it could be Nato’s first line of defence against a Russian attack.” Pevkur announced that he would resign while appearing on an Estonian television programme, public broadcaster ERR reported on Wednesday. He stated that a leader should have the “stature and courage” to take responsibility, even if the fault is not theirs. “As defence minister, I of course have to recognise that I am responsible for the entire area under my ministry, and if you are now waiting for that big answer, then, of course, a leader must have both the courage and the stature to take responsibility as a matter of political responsibility, even when there is no personal responsibility,” Pevkur was quoted as saying by ERR . “I will take that responsibility and the prime minister will have to find a new defence minister.” Pevkur added that he did not look at the contracts, but that his office received them. When asked why he did not read them, he replied that the defence minister “is not responsible for dealing with such details”, ERR added in its report. “The defence minister does not conduct contract negotiations; the defence minister does not count socks and ammunition. The defence minister makes the fundamental decision to support Ukraine. The preparatory work for contract negotiations and finding contracting partners is RKIK’s responsibility,” he was quoted as saying. RKIK, or the Centre for Defence Investments, is Estonia’s central procurement body. Meanwhile, Datasel SRL is suing Estonia on the grounds that it delivered the bulk of the munitions — €59m worth — and would have met its obligations had Estonia not ended the contract, ERR said in a report today. “Datasel is the party that has suffered losses in connection with these supply contracts,” the company told Estonian newspaper Eesti Ekspress through its lawyer. “The actions of the Estonian Centre for Defence Investments, particularly the reasons given for the extraordinary termination of the contracts, are contradictory and illogical,” ERR reports citing the statement.

items.title: Spurs omit Richarlison from Premier League squad
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Tottenham have left Richarlison out of their Premier League squad for the first half of the season as the Brazil forward edges closer to an exit from the club. According to the BBC, Tottenham are braced for a possible approach from Turkish side Trabzonspor after Richarlison’s proposed return to former club Everton fell through before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. The 29-year-old had told Spurs manager Roberto de Zerbi that he wanted to leave, with the Italian confirming last week that the striker had expressed his desire to move on. Sky Sports News also reports that Trabzonspor have yet to formalise their interest, but there is an expectation at Tottenham that the Turkish club could make an approach before the country’s transfer window closes on Friday. Richarlison is also understood not to feature in De Zerbi’s plans this season, with the player informed of the situation before Tuesday’s deadline. The forward could still leave Tottenham in the coming days, with transfer windows in Turkey and Saudi Arabia remaining open. Richarlison joined Spurs from Everton in 2022 and has entered the final year of his contract. He started Tottenham’s Premier League opener against Brentford but was left out of the squad for Saturday’s 2-0 home defeat by Newcastle United. “Richarlison, I don’t know. He said too many times he wants to leave,” De Zerbi said after the Newcastle defeat. Earlier in August, the Spurs boss had acknowledged uncertainty over Richarlison’s future, saying: “It’s not easy to find another striker like Richarlison.” Tottenham have since strengthened their attack with the loan signing of Manchester City striker Omar Marmoush, who replaced Richarlison against Newcastle. Richarlison was Tottenham’s leading Premier League scorer last season, with 11 goals in 32 appearances, while also providing four assists as the club battled to avoid relegation before securing survival on the final day.
